newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries close lower amid threatening data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries close lower amid threatening data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries retraced recent gains on Monday as strong housing sales and an improved Chicago purchasing managers' survey put pressure on the market.
New family home sales rose 7.1 percent in May and the Chicago Purchasing Managers survey increased to 61.5 percent from 56.8 percent from the prior month.
"(Market) sentiment hasn't changed ... we're seeing short covering," said Kevin Flanagan, money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.
"Today's statistics sort of summarize the bond market's quandry," said Fred Sturm, economist at Fuji Securities Inc.
He saw a weakened second quarter possibly followed by hefty growth in the third qwarter, which could prompt the Federal Reserve to again raise short-term interest rates in the third quarter.
Sturm said chances of another tightening at the Federal Open Market Committee's meeting in August was a strong possibility.
"It is the (Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan) Greenspan style to prepare the market, and he hasn't done that yet," Sturm said.

"We expect the Fed to do nothing (at its FOMC meeting)," said Steven Wieting, economist with Smith Barney Inc. Wieting said that even though the Chicago PMI survey looked much stronger, his firm still expected NAPM to remain in current ranges.
He saw the Federal Reserve to refrain from further tightening in July, but still saw two more moves before the end of the year.
"We see GDP growth of 3.0 percent in the third quarter with a serious upside risk," Wieting said. The unemployment rate could drop to 4.7 percent, he added.
GovPX reported that bill volume was 42 percent below volume and coupon volume 41 percent above average.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was trading down 16/32 at 97-31/32 to yield 6.78 percent.
In other trade, the five-year note was off 6/32 at 99-14/32 with a yield of 6.38 percent.

At the short end of the maturity curve, the three-month bill was up four basis points at 5.04 percent and the six-month bill was up three basis points at 5.06 percent. The year bill was up four basis points at 5.36 percent.
